source: Q117 (2026-09-22): generalization of scripts/recount_muscle_gaps.py's exact muscle-completeness method (data/muscles/**/*.json entity ids vs. build/viewer_*/bundle.json structure ids) to every tissue-type data directory under data/ that holds per-entity JSON records with an 'id' field, produced by scripts/recount_tissue_gaps.py. Measurement-only, per PROJECT_STATE Q117: no geometry generated or gaps filled by this item.
method: For each tissue type, every JSON record under its data directory carrying a non-empty 'id' field is one entity (one file per entity for muscles; one list-of-entities per file for every other type audited here). An entity is BOTH if its id appears in both build/viewer_m/bundle.json and build/viewer_f/bundle.json's 'structures' list, EITHER if in exactly one, NEITHER if in neither. base_name() strips a trailing '_l'/'_r' before counting 'distinct' missing structures so a bilateral pair missing on both sides counts once.

measured_against.note: LIVE published bundles only, matching recount_muscle_gaps.py's own convention and Q112's precedent -- NOT the pending Q108-Q116 rebuilds sitting unpublished in build/viewer_*/atlas_viewer_*.html (a different, not-yet-live state).

excluded_data_dirs.data/skeleton/joints.json: 60 kinematic articulation records (DOF ranges, coordinate systems), not mesh entities -- 0 of the 60 ids appear in either bundle by design (a joint has no mesh of its own; it is implied by its adjoining bones). Included as its own line in the per-type table below for transparency, but not counted toward 'bones'.
excluded_data_dirs.data/nerves/spinal_and_cranial_nerve_roo: nested reference table (myotome/dermatome/cranial-nerve lists), no 'id' field on any item -- skipped by the same rule that skips data/muscles/muscle_index.json; matches engine/validators.py's own schema-dispatch comment that this file is 'a reference table, not a nerve_branch entity list'.
excluded_data_dirs.data/ct_sources/: raw CT/cryosection imaging and per-task segmentation outputs, not entity JSON records.
excluded_data_dirs.data/rig/: anchors.json (rig attachment points, keyed by owner_entity) and scene_3d_preview.json are derived rig/viewer-scene data, not their own anatomical entities.
excluded_data_dirs.data/derived/: already-derived audit/report/transfer output, not source entity records.

bones.note: data/skeleton/joints.json deliberately excluded: its 60 records are kinematic articulations (DOF ranges, coordinate systems), not mesh entities -- 0 of its ids appear in either bundle by design, not as a gap (a joint is not rendered as its own mesh; it is implied by its adjoining bones).

bursae.note: one file per joint region, each a list of bursa entities.

cartilage.note: one file per cartilage group, each a list of entities.

fascia.note: one file per body region, each a list of fascia entities.

ligaments.note: one file per joint/region, each a list of ligament entities.

muscles.note: one file per entity (data/muscles/<region>/<name>.json); data/muscles/muscle_index.json is a list with no dict entries and is skipped by the same id-and-dict test.

nerves.note: data/nerves/spinal_and_cranial_nerve_roots.json is a nested reference table (spinal_nerves/cranial_nerves/sources), not an entity list -- its items carry no 'id' field at all and are skipped, matching engine/validators.py's own schema dispatch note that it is 'a reference table, not a nerve_branch entity list'.

tendons.note: one file per body region, each a list of tendon entities.

vascular.note: one file per arterial/venous/lymphatic tree, each a list of vessel entities.

joints.note: 60 kinematic articulation records (DOF ranges, coordinate systems), not mesh entities -- 0 of the 60 ids appear in either bundle by design (a joint has no mesh of its own; it is implied by its adjoining bones). Included as its own line in the per-type table below for transparency, but not counted toward 'bones'.
